chapter: Ellington, singers, the book and closing
title: Death, old ruins and wishing for a good education
summary: He wishes he had had teachers who understood children and a fundamental education.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Yeah. Is there anything I haven't asked you about that you'd like to talk about?
Yeah, man, about death. Look out the window at all these brothers, man, it look like it's always been people here. These brothers look pretty old, some of them.

They go to Europe, you go to India and see all these ruins. I often wonder what this thing is, it's kind of green, that this will be here forever, and it's nothing. Well, the Empire State Building has got to come down pretty soon, right? How old is it now?
It's old. They put it up in the '20s and some big insurance company just bought it. So it could

50 years. I wish I had been born when they had good school teachers, that understood the personalities of children so I could have gotten a good education, because I was a very good reader, and I finally got so I was disgusted to read because I was not good in mathematics.
It was a mystery to me. I wish that -- the main thing, that I got a good education, fundamental education so I could have based my natural talents on that.
And then nothing could have stood in my way. With the same personality, I'm talking about.
